summary: E! plans to launch an as-yet-untitled documentary series about Bruce Jenner's transition on July 26, with eight hour-long episodes. The article identifies several subjects viewers hope it will explore, including Jenner's relationship with former wife Kris, connections with the children, potential role in the transgender community and fans' reactions. Bruce and Kris announced their divorce filing in September 2014 after living separately, and Kris expressed support on Twitter after Jenner's interview with Diane Sawyer on Friday. Jenner has six biological children and helped raise Kris's four children from her first marriage, and told Sawyer that the possibility of hurting the children was a particular concern. The two youngest daughters, Kendall and Kylie, issued a statement emphasizing their love for their father and their wish for Jenner's happiness. Jenner, formerly a motivational speaker as well as an Olympic champion, has already attracted praise for raising awareness of transgender people. GLAAD national co-chair Jennifer Finney Boylan will advise the series, while actress Laverne Cox praised the interview for showing Jenner as a complex human being. As Jenner prepares to become the focus of a new program, public reactions remain a question, but Jenner told Sawyer that the visibility gained through the Kardashian show could provide an opportunity to do good.

Filipinos are being warned to be on guard for flash floods and landslides as tropical storm Maysak, with steady winds of more than 70 mph (115 kph) on Saturday, is expected to make landfall Sunday morning on the southeastern coast of Isabela province and be out of the Philippines by Monday. Authorities took preemptive steps, barring outdoor activities like swimming, surfing, diving and boating in some locales and ordering precautionary evacuations, while Isabela Gov. Faustino Dry III warned that the impact at landfall was unknown.

Yemeni officials said al Qaeda militants raided a prison and seized other government buildings in Al Mukallah early Thursday, freeing at least 270 inmates, a third with al Qaeda ties, including senior figure Khaled Batarfi. Most militants fled after troops clashed with them, officials said, while Yemen's conflict between Houthi rebels and forces loyal to ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi has drawn in Saudi Arabia and Iran, raising the risk of a regional proxy war.

A Transportation Security Administration committee concluded that full screening of airport employees nationwide would not lower the overall risk to the public, according to a report released Monday. The TSA and most airports could not afford 100% employee screening, the report said. As a result of the report, TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions, including criminal background checks every two years for all airport aviation workers, screening of airline and airport employees traveling as passengers, reduction of access points to secure areas at all airports and increased random screening of aviation employees. Johnson requested the TSA study after a Delta Air Lines ramp worker and passenger at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport were arrested in December for allegedly smuggling guns onto flights to New York. Specifically, the TSA report said employee vetting should be strengthened by "updating the list of disqualifying criminal offenses, instituting continuous activity monitoring through the inclusion of additional Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and DHS data sources, and maintaining a national database of airport employees whose credentials have been revoked for cause." In addition, the TSA should expand the collection of domestic intelligence, which would include monitoring social media, and expand national reward programs to encourage employees to report security issues, the report said. Rep. Kathleen Rice, D-New York, a ranking member of the Transportation Security Committee, said the report makes it clear that the "TSA must do more to neutralize the insider threat and prevent security breaches like we saw in December." Lauren Stover, security director at Miami International Airport, told CNN, "We support the findings of the committee and agree that there is no single solution in mitigating the insider threat, however we will continue our employee screening program as we believe that physical screening is a critical component to a layered security program."

Actress Mindy Kaling's brother says that he posed as a black man years ago to get into medical school and that the experience opened his eyes to what he calls the hypocrisy of affirmative action. But a Saint Louis University spokeswoman disputed the account, telling the Huffington Post that race never played a role in Chokal-Ingam's admission.

The Calabrese, an Italian Finance Police ship patrolling the Mediterranean near Lampedusa, has shifted from pursuing cigarette and drug smugglers to helping rescue migrants from Africa and the Middle East with its 12-member crew. During the October 3, 2013, shipwreck off Lampedusa, which killed more than 350 people, its crew saved four survivors. Crew members Gaetano Cortese and Enzo Idone describe enduring memories of recovering dead children, and Cortese recalls retrieving a pregnant woman's body while stressing that they were fulfilling their professional duty. Their well-equipped ship contrasts with the unsafe boats migrants use, often without food, water, shelter or trained crews, after many have already been beaten and robbed.

As Nepal grapples with an earthquake that has killed more than 3,400 people, Ronen Ziv worries about someone he has never met. Ziv says his baby is in a breech position, requiring a cesarean section. In the current chaos of Kathmandu, he worries his surrogate mother, Nafisa Shaje, will not get the proper medical attention required for a safe and healthy birth. Cila Tamir, Ziv's attorney, has been working with the Ministry of the Interior to try to bring Shaje to Israel.

Larry Upright, a staunch Republican, died Monday at a North Carolina hospital at 81, just one day after Hillary Clinton announced she was running for president. In his obituary, his family made just two requests: please donate to Shriners Hospital for Children, and please don't vote for Clinton in 2016. Daughter Jill McLain said it was natural to put that line in her father's tribute because he was very passionate about politics. Son Michael Upright said he knew his father would enjoy the request: "We know he's up there giggling right now, just laughing out loud," he told WSOC. His greatest joy was his family, and he was a former Shriner of the Year at the Cabarrus Shrine Club, according to his obituary. The last few lines of his obituary spurred comments from across the country, including Marina Shear's promise not to vote for Clinton and Ron Renno's pledge to remember the request in November 2016. Nigel Dufont offered his condolences but said he wouldn't budge on his support of Clinton. An anonymous commenter stayed open-minded, saying, "I will vote for Hillary if she is the best candidate."

The new "Fantastic Four" trailer, released Sunday, shows Sue and Johnny Storm's father initiating the project that ends up giving the foursome their powers, the characters entering another dimension and a first glimpse of the villainous Dr. Doom. The movie, due out August 7, promises a very different take on the classic Marvel comics characters, and fans on Twitter had mixed reactions. The new trailer for "Jurassic World," out June 12, came out Monday morning and features Chris Pratt's scientist character taking charge of a mission to contain dangerous creatures after a genetically modified mutant dinosaur escapes from an island theme park along with others. The dinosaurs have learned to communicate with each other, and early word on Twitter was pretty good.
